title: bug: shared frozen-gate integrity never clears skip-worktree, so a gate that hides a tracked edit or deletion behind it records 'passed'
description:
sh gate_integrity and ps1 Clear-MoeGateIndexFlags run ONE `git update-index --no-assume-unchanged --no-skip-worktree -z --stdin`. git applies only the first marking option per path (update_one returns after CE_VALID), so S bits are never cleared.
Repro (git 2.43): commit a.txt; `git update-index --skip-worktree a.txt`; edit or delete it; run the pipe. `ls-files -t` still shows 'S a.txt' and `diff-files --quiet` exits 0, so the run classifies as 'passed'. The postflight hidden-mutation mode passes only because its assume-unchanged gate.cjs edit is caught.
Fix: run two update-index passes (--no-skip-worktree, then --no-assume-unchanged), and add a frozen mode that hides only behind skip-worktree. WT-10G (task-19cbba22) fixed the worktree arm only and left the shared command unchanged under rail 4.
definitionOfDone: A gate that sets skip-worktree on a tracked file and edits or deletes it is classified 'inconclusive' and refused in shared mode, on both wrappers.
postflight.sh and postflight.ps1 carry a byte-identical frozen mode that hides only behind skip-worktree and fails without the fix.
bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh passes and node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs bash exits 0; PS 5.1 postflight passes on the same revision.

implementationPlan.description:
Two marking passes in the shared probe, in scripts/moe-agent.sh.

Read first:
- WT-10G's FINAL landed bytes (task-19cbba22, in rework when this was planned; this row dependsOn it);
- comment-3c560179 on this task;
- mem:gotcha-parity-check-literals.

Root cause. git update-index applies only the FIRST marking option per path: update_one returns after the CE_VALID branch. So `--no-assume-unchanged --no-skip-worktree` never clears S bits, and diff-files then skips a skip-worktree file that was edited or deleted.

Change gate_integrity to run two passes, in this order, each piping the SAME `gate_git ls-files -z "$@"`:
1. `| gate_git update-index --no-skip-worktree -z --stdin || return 1`
2. `| gate_git update-index --no-assume-unchanged -z --stdin || return 1`

Then run the unchanged diff-files check.

error handling: each pass keeps its `|| return 1`. A failed pass is a failed probe: integrity false, then 'inconclusive', and the branch is refused. It never becomes a silent pass.

Both passes MUST pass "$@". The worktree arm calls `gate_integrity -- ':(top,exclude).moe'`; a pass without the exclude would clear the sparse .moe S bits, diff-files would report .moe deleted, and every worktree gate would fail closed (the wt-pass mode).

Move the arm's first-option comment onto these two lines. Then delete gate_integrity_wt's own `--no-skip-worktree` pass, which is now redundant (comment-3c560179). Keep its .moe presence check and its `gate_integrity -- ':(top,exclude).moe'` call, exactly as WT-10G landed them.

That removal is deliberate. The wt-hidden mode (skip-worktree + delete) and the wt-assume mode (assume-unchanged + edit) then exercise the shared probe's two passes, one mutant each.

Check with `bash -n scripts/moe-agent.sh`. Edit only with the main session's Edit tool (global rail).
implementationPlan.note: gate_integrity now runs two passes over the same `ls-files -z "$@"`: `update-index --no-skip-worktree -z --stdin || return 1`, then `update-index --no-assume-unchanged -z --stdin || return 1`, then the unchanged diff-files. The first-option comment moved onto these lines. gate_integrity_wt lost its redundant arm-local S pass; its .moe presence check and `gate_integrity -- ':(top,exclude).moe'` call are byte-identical to WT-10G's landed bytes (14f546ea/1feb9c0b). bash -n OK. implementationPlan.description:
The same fix in scripts/moe-agent.ps1. Keep the file UTF-8 with a BOM.

- **Test-MoeGateIntegrity.** Replace its one `Clear-MoeGateIndexFlags $top $Exclude` call with two calls, in this order, each with $Exclude:
  1. `Clear-MoeGateIndexFlags $top $Exclude 'update-index --no-skip-worktree -z --stdin'`
  2. `Clear-MoeGateIndexFlags $top $Exclude 'update-index --no-assume-unchanged -z --stdin'`
  Each literal is passed WHOLE, so parity-check finds it (mem:gotcha-parity-check-literals).
- **error handling.** Each call returns $false from Test-MoeGateIntegrity when it fails (a non-zero cmd exit, or a caught exception inside Clear-MoeGateIndexFlags). The caller's existing try/catch, which treats a throw as integrity false (CQ-V04c), stays unchanged.
- **Clear-MoeGateIndexFlags.** Remove the default value of its $Update parameter, so no caller can silently fall back to the broken combined pass. Every caller now passes the whole tail. Keep the cmd-pipe raw-bytes mechanism, the EAP handling and the Push/Pop-Location unchanged.
- **Test-MoeGateIntegrityWorktree.** Delete its now-redundant `--no-skip-worktree` pre-pass. Keep the .moe Get-Item -Force presence check and the `Test-MoeGateIntegrity $Frozen ':(top,exclude).moe'` call. Move the first-option comment onto Test-MoeGateIntegrity.

Check that the file parses with zero errors under both engines, for example `[System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile` with powershell.exe and with pwsh.exe, and that `head -c3 scripts/moe-agent.ps1 | od -An -tx1` prints `ef bb bf`.
implementationPlan.note: Test-MoeGateIntegrity now calls Clear-MoeGateIndexFlags twice with $Exclude and whole literals: 'update-index --no-skip-worktree -z --stdin', then 'update-index --no-assume-unchanged -z --stdin'; each `{ return $false }` on failure (cmd exit != 0 or the helper's caught exception), so a failed pass is integrity false. The first-option comment moved here. Clear-MoeGateIndexFlags lost both parameter defaults ($Exclude='' and the combined $Update literal); a caller omitting $Update would run `git ` alone and fail closed. Its cmd-pipe, EAP and Push/Pop-Location are unchanged. Test-MoeGateIntegrityWorktree lost its arm-local S pass; presence check and `Test-MoeGateIntegrity $Frozen ':(top,exclude).moe'` unchanged. Checks: BOM `ef bb bf`; ParseFile errors=0 under powershell.exe 5.1.26100 and pwsh.exe 7.6.9. No other caller of Clear-MoeGateIndexFlags exists (grep scripts/ docs/).

New frozen mode `skip-worktree-mutation` (both harnesses, +3/-0 gate body plus the mode added beside hidden-mutation in all 5 lists: modes array, `failed`, PUSH-BLOCKED, wantOutcome 'inconclusive', and the one-check/exit-0/'inconclusive' block). Suite cmp (FROZENJS vs $frozenSuite) OK; postflight.ps1 keeps its BOM; bash -n postflight.sh OK.

comments.author: worker-009c883d
comments.content:
How this fix interacts with WT-10G (task-19cbba22, filed by its worker):
- The worktree arm's gate_integrity_wt (sh) / Test-MoeGateIntegrityWorktree (ps1) runs its own skip-worktree pass first: `ls-files -z -- ':(top,exclude).moe' | update-index --no-skip-worktree -z --stdin` (ps1: Clear-MoeGateIndexFlags ... '--no-skip-worktree').
- After that it calls the shared probe with the same exclude pathspec. sh gate_integrity passes "$@" to ls-files; ps1 uses Test-MoeGateIntegrity's $Exclude.

When you split the shared pipe into two passes, apply "$@" / $Exclude to BOTH of them. Otherwise the arm would clear the .moe/ S bits, diff-files would see .moe/ as deleted, and every worktree gate would fail closed. That case is the wt-pass mode.

Once both passes honor the exclude, the arm's extra skip-worktree line is redundant and can go. The wt-hidden mode (skip-worktree + delete) still has to fail afterwards.
